After months of testing Liquid Glass, WhatsApp is expanding user access to its redesigned iPad app interface, including a brand new Mac-like sidebar. Here's what you need to know.

WhatsApp is developing a brand new iPad app interface

WhatsApp began working on the Liquid Glass visual overhaul for its iOS app as early as last October, but the company later brought this redesign to the iPad first, starting limited beta testing in June.

At the time, WABetaInfo reported that the redesign included Liquid Glass-style tabs, buttons, and action menus, while retaining the familiar bottom tab bar found on iPhone.

WABetaInfo is now reporting that WhatsApp is rolling out another major interface change for some iPad users, replacing the bottom tab bar by default with a brand new Mac-like sidebar.

This sidebar mirrors the layout of the existing WhatsApp Mac app, providing quick access to Chats, Updates, Communities, Calls, Meta AI, and other app sections. Users can also collapse it to give the conversation list and chat window more display space.

WABetaInfo reports as follows:

WABetaInfo notes that some beta testers in the latest TestFlight build already have access to the new sidebar, while some users on the regular App Store version are also beginning to see the change.

As is typical with WhatsApp, the new interface may take some time to roll out to all users, whether they are on the beta or the official version. However, once iPad users receive the update, they can benefit from a layout better suited for tablet use.
